items.informal_name: Composition of Taylor Expansions: $ T_r(T_s(f)) = T_{r+s}(f) $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : Polynomial R) (r s : R),
  (Polynomial.taylor r) ((Polynomial.taylor s) f) = (Polynomial.taylor (r + s)) f
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ f \in R[X] $ and elements $ r, s \in R $, composing the Taylor series expansion at $ r $ with the Taylor series expansion at $ s $ yields the same result as the Taylor series expansion at $ r + s $. Formally, $ \operatorname{taylor}_r(\operatorname{taylor}_s f) = \operatorname{taylor}_{r+s} f $. This expresses the additive property of Taylor shifts in polynomial rings over semirings.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (r : R) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.taylor r) f = f.comp (Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C r)
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ f $ in $ R[X] $ and any element $ r $ in the semiring $ R $, the Taylor expansion of $ f $ at $ r $ is equal to the composition of $ f $ with the polynomial $ X + r $, i.e., $ \text{Tay}_r(f) = f(X + r) $, where $ X $ denotes the indeterminate of the polynomial ring.

items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → R → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a given element $ r $ in a semiring $ R $, the Taylor series expansion at $ r $ is the $ R $-linear map from $ R[X] $ to $ R[X] $ that sends each polynomial $ f $ to the composition $ f(X + r) $.

items.informal_name: Taylor Expansion Evaluation Identity: $(\mathrm{taylor}\, r\, f)(s) = f(s + r)$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (r : R) (f : Polynomial R) (s : R),
  Polynomial.eval s ((Polynomial.taylor r) f) = Polynomial.eval (s + r) f
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ f \in R[X] $ and elements $ r, s \in R $, the evaluation of the Taylor expansion of $ f $ at $ r $ at $ s $ equals $ f(s + r) $.

items.informal_name: Taylor Series Expansion at r is R-Linear
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_2} {S : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : Semiring S] (p : Polynomial R) (r : R) (f : R →+* S),
  Polynomial.map f ((Polynomial.taylor r) p) = (Polynomial.taylor (f r)) (Polynomial.map f p)
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a semiring $ R $, the Taylor series expansion at $ r $ is an $ R $-linear map from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself, which sends each polynomial $ f $ to the polynomial obtained by substituting $ X + r $ into $ f $.

items.informal_name: Taylor Isomorphism for Polynomials over Commutative Rings
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (r : R), (Polynomial.taylorEquiv r).symm = Polynomial.taylorEquiv (-r)
items.informal_description: For any element $ r $ in a commutative ring $ R $, the Taylor isomorphism is an $ R $-algebra isomorphism from the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ to itself that maps each polynomial $ f(X) $ to $ f(X + r) $. This equivalence preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, with the inverse map given by substituting $ X - r $.

This equivalence preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication, with the inverse map given by substituting $ X - r $.

items.informal_name: The Taylor Shift Operator: Algebra Homomorphism vs. Linear Map
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (r : R) (a : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.taylorAlgHom r) a = (Polynomial.taylor r) a
items.informal_description:
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $r \in R$, and $p$ a polynomial over $R$. Then
$$ (\text{Polynomial.taylorAlgHom } r)(p) = (\text{Polynomial.taylor } r)(p) $$
Here, `Polynomial.taylorAlgHom r` and `Polynomial.taylor r` are the Taylor shift operator $p(X) \mapsto p(X+r)$, viewed as an $R$-algebra homomorphism and an $R$-linear map, respectively.
